To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) chaotic fluctuations emerge from the interaction of single neuron nonlinearities and recurrent connectivity and (b) chaotic fluctuations can be used to transmit information in a network.

(1) the power spectrum of chaotic network activity in random neural networks emerges from a nonlinear enhancement of the frequency response of single neurons, and (2) adaptation in single units enhances the transmission of weak low frequency signals in the chaotic state.

the chaotic dynamics in random neural networks emerge from the interaction between single neuron properties and recurrent connectivity, and that these networks can be in a state of resonant chaos characterized by a narrow band of stochastic oscillations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the dynamics of large randomly connected neural networks.
the dynamics and function of random networks of spiking neurons.
the analysis of complex dynamical systems, which is a central problem in physics and mathematics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dynamics of single neurons, in particular the adaptation dynamics, can shape the chaotic dynamics and the transmission of weak signals in large random neural networks, which is a key ingredient for the understanding of neural information processing.

the dynamics of a large randomly connected network is a nonlinear transformation of the frequency response of the single neurons, and that this transformation can be understood in terms of the dynamical mean field approach, which is a generalization of the mean field approach for spin glasses.
the chaotic phase is a dynamical regime where neurons are maximally responsive to weak inputs and maximally sensitive to the properties of the single neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the dynamics of a single neuron is a crucial factor in determining the dynamical properties (such as the onset of chaos, the power spectrum, the correlation time, the signal transmission) of a network of randomly connected neurons.

the chaotic fluctuations in the activity of a random network emerge as the result of a non-linear sharpening of the intrinsic dynamics of individual units and that the chaotic fluctuations enhance the transmission of weak signals in the network.
the dynamical mean field approach can be applied to a broad range of single neuron models with complex dynamics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chaotic dynamics of a single neuron can be used as a building block to construct chaotic dynamics at the population level.

the dynamical properties that single neurons exhibit in the absence of synaptic input can have a profound impact on the effective dynamics of large networks and the transmission of signals in the presence of noise.
the dynamical properties at the level of individual neurons can be used to predict the dynamical behavior of the network as a whole.
